claims.text: 29 Nov 1983 agreement created the Joint Political-Military Group (JPMG) and Joint Security Assistance Planning Group (JSAP); JPMG first on Soviet threats, later chemical weapons and missile proliferation; JSAP meets annually in Washington to review Israel's procurement and FMS credit. 23 Jan 1987 MNNA; April 1988 MOA institutionalized the relationship. Haifa hosts around 40 US Navy ships a year; USS Iwo Jima docked in Haifa March 2018 after Juniper Cobra.

WRSA-I: begun in the 1980s under an MOU; FAA s.514 cap on additions $200m/yr (CRS: stock value up to $4.4bn); DoD holds title; Israel pays storage/maintenance; oversight moved EUCOM→CENTCOM Sept 2021; bilateral agreement classified. 2006: PGMs transferred during Lebanon war; 2014: 120mm tank and 40mm illumination rounds via a $3m FMS case, Pentagon called it 'routine', White House reportedly unaware; 2023: US moved 300,000 155mm shells out of WRSA-I for Ukraine, promised replenishment, reporting said final approval rested with Israel's PM. FY2021 NDAA s.1275 allows PGM transfers outside the cap, extended to 2027 by FY2024 NDAA s.1255. 20 Oct 2023 supplemental request sought to lift the cap.
Jan 2023: about half of an expected 300,000 155mm rounds from the Israel stockpile had reportedly reached Ukraine (NYT).
Oct–Nov 2008 the US deployed an X-band radar to the Negev with 120 US personnel, to detect missiles such as Iran's Shahab-3, linked to Israeli and US missile-defence systems.

Site 512, Mt Har Qeren in the Negev about 20 miles from Gaza: classified US radar facility focused on Iran; 2 Aug 2023 Pentagon contract announcement $35.8m for a 'life support facility'; described as 'classified worldwide' project. JVL (citing Time 2012) says it houses the AN/TPY-2 radar and gives Israel minutes of extra warning.

Juniper Cobra 2018 (ninth biennial edition, concluded 15 Mar 2018): more than 2,500 US and about 2,000 Israeli personnel, ballistic missile defence interoperability. Juniper Oak 23.2 (ended 26 Jan 2023): about 6,400 US and 1,500+ Israeli troops, 140+ aircraft incl B-52, F-35, F-15, F-16, F/A-18, AC-130, AH-64, USS George H.W. Bush CSG; CENTCOM: largest partnered exercise; Kurilla quote.

13 Oct 2024 DoD: Austin, at the President's direction, authorized a THAAD battery and crew to Israel after Iran's 13 April and 1 October attacks; US 'previously deployed a THAAD battery to Israel in 2019 for training'. AP: a battery generally needs 95 soldiers (CRS); Ryder: 'ironclad commitment to the defense of Israel'.

Army announced Aug 2018 it would buy Iron Dome as interim cruise-missile defence; bought two batteries 2019, delivered late 2020–early 2021; one temporarily deployed to Guam; Army bought no more partly due to networking problems; Oct 2023 reports said DoD would lease both back to Israel; Ryder said Tamir interceptors delivered came from Army stocks.

F-35: 7 Oct 2010 Israel signed for 20 F-35s (~$3bn) funded by US aid; total 50 ordered by Nov 2016; designated F-35I 'Adir' for unique Israeli features: Elbit EW equipment (2012 contract), IAI command-and-control software layer, Israeli weapons, helmet displays made in Israel; US initially refused own EW integration; first combat use announced 22 May 2018; Lockheed pledged ~$4bn purchases from Israeli firms; IAI makes wings.

13–14 Apr 2024: of 300+ Iranian/proxy air threats, US forces incl destroyers USS Arleigh Burke and USS Carney (EUCOM) destroyed more than 80 one-way attack drones and at least six ballistic missiles aimed at Israel (Ryder, 15 Apr 2024). 1 Oct 2024: destroyers USS Bulkeley and USS Cole fired about a dozen interceptors against ~200 Iranian ballistic missiles.
June 2025 12-day war: US fired more than 100, possibly 150, THAAD interceptors, about a quarter of its supply, using two of seven THAAD systems (CNN, 28 Jul 2025).

8 Oct 2023 Austin ordered USS Gerald R. Ford CSG (cruiser Normandy, five destroyers) to eastern Mediterranean and augmented F-35, F-15, F-16, A-10 squadrons; to deter regional widening; extra munitions to Israel.

28 Feb 2026 US and Israel launched coordinated strikes on Iran (US 'Epic Fury', Israel 'Roaring Lion') with 'full synchronization and coordination'; Iran state media confirmed Khamenei killed; Trump said aim to remove imminent threats; ceasefire 7–8 Apr 2026, extended, Islamabad Memorandum 17 Jun, collapsed 8 Jul 2026.

CENTCOM estimate (as of 3 Sep 2026, AP 18 Sep 2026): $43.6bn US cost of Iran war, munitions 'well over half'; CBO $38bn through 1 Aug; interceptors (Patriot, THAAD) most demanded. Pentagon DCAS (Oct 2026): 21 troops died in operations against Iran, 865 wounded.
